o: An array is 'positive' if every subarray of length ≥ 3 has a strictly positive sum. Using prefix sums P where P[0]=0, a subarray (l, r] has non-positive sum exactly when P[r+1] ≤ P[l] with r+1-l ≥ 3. So the array is positive iff for every k ≥ 3, P[k] > min(P[0..k-3]). An operation replaces one element with any value in [-10¹⁸, 10¹⁸]; increasing an element only increases every subarray sum containing it, so replacements should always raise a value (never lower one). Example 1 needs 1 op (fix the whole array's sum); Example 3 needs 0.
k: Positivity ⟺ for every k ≥ 3: P[k] > min(P[0..k-3]) over prefix sums.
Raising an element never breaks any constraint, so all edits are increases.
When a violation appears at prefix k, editing the element achieving the minimal prefix in the allowed range fixes it and helps all future windows.

a.i: Find the leftmost violated prefix k, locate the index i ≤ k-3 with minimum prefix value, and set nums[i] to 10¹⁸. Increasing that element lifts every subsequent prefix, fixing the violation and helping future ones. Repeat until no violation exists.
s: Compute prefix sums of the current array.
Find the smallest k ≥ 3 with P[k] ≤ min(P[0..k-3]); if none, stop.
Set nums[argmin over P[0..k-3]] = 10¹⁸, increment the counter, repeat.
a.t: O(n²) worst case — each round is O(n) and there are at most n rounds; fast in practice.

a.i: Simulate the same greedy in one sweep. Index i enters the 'allowed range' when the scan reaches k = i+3, at which point (P[i], i) is pushed to a min-heap. At each k, the heap top is min(P[0..k-3]); if P[k] ≤ that value we perform one edit and mark that index used (lazy-deleted from the heap) since its element is now effectively infinite.
s: For k = 3..n: push (P[k-3], k-3); pop used tops; if P[k] ≤ top value, count an edit and mark top index used.
a.t: O(n log n) — each index is pushed and popped at most once.
a.sp: O(n) — prefix sums, heap, and used flags.

w: Lead with the prefix-sum characterization; the heap version is the clean O(n log n) interview answer. Pitfalls: forgetting that subarrays of ALL lengths ≥ 3 matter (checking only length-3 windows is wrong, e.g. [-10,6,5,-1]); using 32-bit sums (values reach 10¹⁸); decreasing an element can never help. Follow-up: what if replacements were limited to a smaller range — then exact amounts matter and a DP is needed.
